security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed one real external-command concern: SKILL.md line 49 instructs agents to run a Python ledger command with user-provided domain and keyword data. The remaining code-fence, URL, and relative-link findings are documentation false positives. I found no prompt injection or hidden data-exfiltration intent in the reviewed SKILL.md content.

remediation.issue: The ledger workflow describes a shell command that includes user-provided domain and keyword values.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the inline shell command with a host-managed action, or require argument-array execution with strict domain and keyword validation.

remediation.issue: The declared allowed tool list does not include local command execution for the ledger workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Align the allowed tools with the workflow, or remove the command and ask users to provide ranking exports manually.

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 23-25 are a Markdown prompt example inside a fenced block. They do not contain executable Ruby or shell logic.
Lines 25-27 only close one Markdown example and open another. No command invocation or dynamic execution is present.
Lines 27-29 contain a natural-language usage example in a Markdown fence. This is not backtick command execution.
The detected backticks are Markdown formatting around examples and section text. There is no executable command at this location.
Line 33 formats the path memory/monitoring as inline code in documentation. It does not execute a shell command.
The line 37 snippet is documentation for a memory file path. The executable ledger example later in the range is covered by the separate line 49 finding.

Line 49 instructs the agent to run a Python ledger command with user-provided domain and keyword data. This is a real external-command workflow that needs input validation and non-shell argument handling.
The cited range uses inline code for file paths and labels such as CLAUDE.md and memory/monitoring. It does not add another executable command.
Line 10 is a homepage metadata URL pointing to the source repository. It is not a network request or exfiltration endpoint.
Line 14 embeds the same repository homepage in metadata. It does not instruct the agent to send data to that URL.
Line 39 is a fixed Markdown link to a neighboring skill document. It is not user-controlled path traversal.
Line 43 is a fixed relative documentation link to a shared skill contract. No file read or write is performed from user input.
Line 47 references CONNECTORS.md through a fixed documentation link. The path is not constructed from user input.
The path traversal pattern on line 49 appears in fixed Markdown reference links. The separate command-execution concern on this line is covered by the external_commands verdict.
Line 96 uses a fixed memory/monitoring output directory and a fixed documentation link. It asks before saving and does not accept an arbitrary path.
Line 104 contains fixed relative links to the next skill and the shared contract. These are documentation references, not traversal through user input.
Line 49 records and compares ranking snapshots for a user-specified domain. It does not gather host system information or enumerate local resources.

content.user_title: Track SEO Rankings and SERP Movement
content.value_statement: Ranking changes are hard to explain when snapshots, baselines, and sources are mixed. This skill structures keyword, SERP feature, competitor, and AI visibility tracking into source-labeled reports.
actual_capabilities: Configures tracking scope by domain, market, device, language, update frequency, and competitors.
Builds current ranking snapshots with keyword positions, target URLs, source labels, and movement against a baseline.
Compares position changes across periods and separates wins, declines, new rankings, and lost rankings.
Tracks SERP feature ownership, AI Overview presence, citation rate, and competitor visibility when data exists.
Produces ranking performance reports with risks, opportunities, and recommended next actions.
limitations: It does not collect live rankings unless approved connectors or user-provided exports are available.
It cannot prove the cause of ranking changes without supporting technical, content, and competitor evidence.
Alert setup and broad stakeholder reporting belong in a performance-monitor workflow.
Manual search results may vary by location, personalization, device, and search engine changes.

use_cases.title: Monitor Priority Keywords
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable ranking snapshot for important keywords, markets, devices, and competitors.

use_cases.title: Review Content Launch Impact
use_cases.description: Compare rankings before and after a content update, then identify wins, losses, and next actions.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitive Movement
use_cases.description: Track competitor gains, SERP feature ownership, and visibility threats across shared keyword sets.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Rank Tracking
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup with a known domain and keyword list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up rank tracking for [domain] in [market] on [device]. Use these keywords: [keyword list]. Include competitors and priority tiers.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Ranking Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review with current and previous ranking data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze ranking changes for [domain] from [start date] to [end date]. Use my export and label every metric as measured, user-provided, or estimated.

prompt_templates.title: Audit SERP and AI Visibility
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced visibility review across classic SERP and AI results.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review SERP features and AI Overview visibility for [domain]. Compare feature ownership, citation rate, competitors, and content gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Recovery Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced response to important ranking losses.
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate ranking drops for [domain] across [keyword group]. Separate likely technical, content, competitor, and SERP causes. Recommend actions by urgency.

output_examples.input: Track example.com for ten product keywords in the United States on mobile.
output: Tracking setup: domain, market, device, language, keyword priorities, target URLs, and competitors.
Current snapshot: keyword positions, ranking URLs, SERP features, and source labels.
Next check: weekly tracking with baseline comparison after the first measured snapshot.

output_examples.input: Analyze last month's ranking drops from our exported keyword list.
output: Movement summary: biggest declines, stable terms, new rankings, and lost rankings.
Cause hypotheses: technical, content, competitor, and SERP feature factors marked as unconfirmed.
Action plan: immediate checks, content updates, competitor review, and monitoring priorities.

output_examples.input: Compare our AI Overview visibility with two competitors.
output: AI visibility summary: presence, citation rate, citation position, and missing source signals.
Competitor comparison: where each domain is cited, absent, or losing feature ownership.
Recommendations: pages to strengthen, facts to source, and queries to monitor.

best_practices: Keep one baseline per market, device, language, and search engine.
Label every metric as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
Compare drops against competitors and holdout keywords before assigning cause.
anti_patterns: Do not report movement without a current snapshot and a baseline.
Do not mix mobile, desktop, or markets in one trend line.
Do not treat estimated AI visibility as measured data.

faq.question: Does this skill fetch live rankings?
faq.answer: Only when an approved connector or export is available. Otherwise it asks for user-provided ranking data.

faq.question: Can it use Search Console data?
faq.answer: Yes, if the user provides exports or an approved connector supplies Search Console metrics.

faq.question: Does it create alerts?
faq.answer: No. Use a performance-monitor workflow when recurring alerts or stakeholder reporting are required.

faq.question: Can it track AI Overview citations?
faq.answer: Yes, it can structure AI visibility checks and label values as measured or unavailable.

faq.question: How does it handle missing baseline data?
faq.answer: It records the current run as the first snapshot and avoids inventing previous positions.

faq.question: Can it explain why rankings changed?
faq.answer: It provides evidence-based hypotheses, but it does not claim causes without supporting data.
